findings.title: Blocked addresses can be bypassed by changing email case
findings.body: The lookup compares the submitted value to `blocked_emails.email` verbatim and neither this model nor `User.new_from_params` canonicalizes email addresses. On the supported case-sensitive database, a block for `person@example.com` will not match a signup using `person@EXAMPLE.COM`, even though email domains are case-insensitive and both forms deliver to the same mailbox. This also permits differently cased duplicate block-list entries with conflicting actions. Normalize and strip emails consistently when storing and querying (and enforce normalized uniqueness, ideally at the database level).

findings.title: Match statistics are lost under concurrent validations
findings.body: `should_block?` performs a read-modify-write of `match_count` in application memory. Two simultaneous signup validations can both read the same count, increment it, and save the same next value, so one match is lost; an older request can also overwrite a newer `last_match_at`. The feature explicitly records these statistics, so this produces inaccurate audit data under normal concurrent traffic. Update these fields atomically in SQL (for example, `match_count = match_count + 1` together with `last_match_at`) rather than incrementing a loaded record.
